_comment: Resolved Spread the Sign (en.in — Indian Sign Language) pages for each dictionary term, checked one by one against their search. Used by `npm run sign:links`. Hand-maintained; the sync script never rewrites this file.

_confidence.direct: The word's own entry, meaning matches. Still worth an eyeball.
_confidence.sense: Several entries share the spelling, or the money sense sits under a compound. Pick deliberately — the wrong one teaches the wrong sign.
_confidence.none: No entry in the Indian Sign Language section. Source from ISLRTC or film it. `nearest` is a related word, NOT a substitute.

note.note: Use BANKNOTE. The plain 'note' entries (7632, 16094, 21415) are note-as-in-write-something-down, which is a different sign and the wrong lesson.

account.note: BANK ACCOUNT matches the definition. Plain 'account' (12326) can mean an online login or a narrative.

deposit.note: BANK DEPOSIT. Plain 'deposit' (8238, 15708) also covers a rental deposit and a geological one.

withdrawal.note: Only the verb WITHDRAW exists. Every noun 'withdrawal' entry is medical — withdrawal symptom, drug withdrawal. Check the verb is the money sense before using it.

need.note: The noun (9553), not the verb (515). The entry teaches need-as-a-thing-you-must-have.

save.note: Two verb entries, 8088 and 25727. Watch both: one is likely save-money, the other save-a-life or save-a-file.

interest.note: Three entries — 576 is the verb (to interest someone), 15833 and 25156 are nouns. INTEREST RATE (5511) may be the clearer money sense for this lesson.

balance.note: Four entries. 5460 and 20628 are nouns, 12369 and 20627 verbs (to balance / stay steady). Only one means money-in-the-account.

rupee.note: No entry. CURRENCY is generic, not the rupee. This one probably has a well-known local sign — ask a Deaf ISL user first.

savings-goal.note: No entry. A compound phrase; likely signed as SAVE + GOAL rather than a single sign.

compound-interest.note: No entry. Likely INTEREST plus an explanation rather than one sign.

pin.note: Entries exist but all are the sewing/bowling kind. Nothing for a card PIN — usually fingerspelled.

upi.note: No entry. India-specific and recent; usually fingerspelled.

scam.note: No entry for 'scam'. FRAUD is close but more formal than what a child would be taught.
